title: Coordinate models and shift comparisons for DG bimodule tensor and Hom
statement:
Use the integer cochain DG algebras, right modules, underlying complexes, quasi-isomorphisms and standard derived localizations of [def-sfb-dg-derived-category]. Let A and B be associative unital DG algebras over Z and let N be an (A,B)-bimodule: a complex with unital associative chain-map actions A tensor N to N and N tensor B to N satisfying the commuting-actions square. This is Mathlib's monoidal bimodule notion. Write rho_M for a right module's chain action and evaluate actions using the inclusions of homogeneous pure tensors. A degree-r cochain f:X to Y is right B-linear if f(xb)=f(x)b for all homogeneous x,b, with no sign. A right DG B-module I is homotopically injective if, for every acyclic right DG B-module C, every closed homogeneous right B-linear cochain C to I in every integer degree r is the differential of a right B-linear cochain in degree r-1, where delta(f)=d_I f-(-1)^r f d_C.
A balanced tensor model for a functor F:Mod(A) to Mod(B) is a natural chain map pi_M:M tensor_Z N to F(M) exhibiting its underlying complex as the coequalizer of rho_M tensor 1 and (1 tensor actLeft) after reassociation, whose right B-action is induced by actRight on N. Thus this model specifies exactly the balanced tensor, with direct-sum totalization and differential d(m tensor n)=d(m) tensor n+(-1)^|m| m tensor d(n).
A bimodule Hom model for G:Mod(B) to Mod(A) consists, in every degree r and at every Y, of an injective linear coordinate map from G(Y)^r onto all homogeneous right B-linear degree-r cochains N to Y. Coordinates intertwine the differential delta, the action (fa)(n)=f(an), and postcomposition by every morphism Y to Y'. An ordinary adjunction F left-adjoint to G is currying when its transpose sends g to m mapping to n mapping to g(pi_M(m tensor n)).
For a shift S isomorphic to M[k] as in [def-sfb-dg-derived-category], a tensor model's shift comparison F(S) isomorphic to F(M)[k] is sign free on pi(m tensor n), shifting the M element. A Hom model's shift comparison G(S) isomorphic to G(Y)[k], for S isomorphic to Y[k], is sign free on every homogeneous coordinate, shifting its output. These definitions are universal-property and coordinate specifications; no existence or adjunction theorem is part of them.
